field.body:
## Field report: #203 closed by PR #207 (merged as ee398fcf)

**Consequence.** On Windows, a slow opaque management test is now reported as an ordinary named test failure, still red. It no longer aborts the whole `telex_watcher` lib harness with 0xc0000409 and hides the failure. The test's hang guard is now 60 s (`DURABLE_MANAGEMENT_HANG_GUARD`), sized to the measured hosted durations, so the known 10 s overrun no longer fails it.

**What held**
- The root cause was proven on a hosted runner. Stress run 40280833707, shard 5, reproduced the crash, and an attached `procdump -e` dump showed the mechanism:
  1. The opaque test's `timeout(10s).unwrap()` panicked.
  2. `Fixture::drop` then ran `remove_dir_all().expect()`, which failed because the detached owner task still held `registry.sqlite` open.
  3. That second panic during unwinding led to an abort and `__fastfail(7)`, which is 0xc0000409.
  Full write-up: https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/issues/203#issuecomment-6411706945
- Hosted timing run 40293264090 (8 shards, 1,054 iterations, 3,162 measured runs) had 0 crashes and 0 failures. The guarded section took p50 0.5 s, p99 3.1 s, max 7.4 s. Registry open alone reached 14.7 s. There were no lock waits.
- Exact-head CI at 712eb6d3 (run 40328958226): 21/21 after one rerun of an unrelated failure, recorded on #193 (https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/issues/193#issuecomment-6417280525). The Windows watcher lib harness passed 60, failed 0, ignored 1.
- Main CI at merge ee398fcf (run 40332382383): 21/21 on the first attempt. The Windows watcher lib harness passed 60, failed 0, ignored 1.
- Independent exact-head source-review receipts:
  - https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/pull/207#issuecomment-6416881499 (776d65d6)
  - https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/pull/207#issuecomment-6416957121 (712eb6d3)

**What changed**
- The `Fixture` Drop in three watcher test modules (runtime_management_tests, registry_tests, transport/tests) now skips its cleanup `expect` while the thread is already panicking.
- A new regression test, `fixture_cleanup_failure_while_unwinding_preserves_the_original_panic`, checks that the original panic survives a failed cleanup.
- Both opaque-test timeouts were raised from 10 s to the 60 s `DURABLE_MANAGEMENT_HANG_GUARD`.
- The Mio 1.2.4 bump (#196) is not the #203 cause, and #203 was not closed on its account.

**Discoveries and disposition**
- **Fail-fast capture on hosted runners.** Only an attached `procdump -e` captured this `__fastfail` abort; WER LocalDumps and AeDebug captured nothing. Routed to Local Daemon / test sentinel. The recipe is at commit 51ab3c6f, `.github/diag-203/setup-capture.ps1`.
- **tokio-rs/mio#2014 defect state** was hit in the CLI and InstalledCurrent harnesses. This is not the #203 cause. Recorded under #166: https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/issues/166#issuecomment-6416861305

**Deferred work**
1. The reverted-fix reproduction (the regression test exits 0xc0000409 without the guard) ran locally only, not on a hosted runner.
2. Why CI exceeded the 10 s bound is unexplained. Hosted timing shows slow `synchronous=FULL` SQLite I/O with no lock waits. The underlying disk or fsync latency source has not been isolated.
3. `telex-watcher/tests/cli_v2.rs:101-103`: its `Fixture` Drop has the same `remove_dir_all(...).expect(...)` hazard while unwinding.
4. `telex-watcher/src/transport/tests.rs` uses 3 s `timeout(...)` bounds that were not sized against hosted latency.
5. When a test fails, its fixture root is now left in the temp directory, because cleanup is best effort while unwinding.

**Process note.** Local runs got no gate credit. Diagnosis and clearance rest only on hosted evidence; the local reverted-fix reproduction is recorded as process debt (item 1).

**Reopen condition.** If the `telex_watcher` lib harness exits 0xc0000409 again, reopen #203.

evidence.body:
Design steward decision: how #199, #200 and #201 treat background work. This follows the #198 owner's observation (#198 comment 6402709899, recorded in ADR 0056 on #202).

**Finding.** A session that ends its turn while a background shell runs looks idle in its log, because the shell's tool call completes at launch. Background agents are unverified. The App may also show such a session as idle, so the design must not rely on the root's App confirmation to catch this case.

**Decision.** The stall condition stays as designed, and background work remains a wake source. What changes is how each item handles it:

- **#199 (detector).** Count background work as a wake source only where the detector can observe it with evidence. It may investigate a bounded, read-only source, such as the session's live child processes, but is not required to. Where background work is not observed, the stall event's snapshot must say so for each member, so the root does not read it as confirmed absence. No parsing of tool result text and no guessing from timing.
- **#200 (guidance).** A member that ends a turn to wait on a background shell or agent sets its own state to parked with a reason, and back to active when woken. On a stall event the root confirms, then rings. A member that is rung while legitimately waiting replies with what it is waiting for and stays parked.
- **#201 (gate).** Add one staged case: an active member idle while its background shell runs. It passes if no stall is reported (when #199 observes background work), or if the event marks background work as unobserved and the root's ring gets the member's reply without disturbing the work.

**Why.** A false stall costs one ring to an idle member. A missed stall leaves the workstream sitting still, which is the failure this design exists to prevent. A reported stall that the root checks is the better error.

This does not change the graph: the four items, their order, their dependencies and the stall-detection-validated checkpoint are unchanged, and nothing is narrowed. The open questions above are unchanged.

evidence.body:
Design steward input for #199, from the #198 owner's follow-up sample (#198 comment 6402770548): all seven unknowns came from `session.start` (six) and `session.error` (one).

`session.error` matters most. A member whose last event is an error has probably stopped and is waiting for input. That is a common reason for a group to stall. Today it classifies as unknown, unknown makes the detector degraded, and a degraded run reaches no one. So one errored member could silently hold off stall detection for its whole group.

Requirement for #199: a member left quiet after `session.error` must not silently suppress alerting. Either recognize it with evidence, as its own reason, so the stall condition can count it, or make sure the root hears about it. The owner chooses the mechanism. The same applies to a member that stays at `session.start` with no later activity, though kickoff prompts make that rare. This partly answers the open question in #197 about persistent unknown: unknown may still mean degraded, but it must not hide a stuck member indefinitely.

Nothing changes in #198, the graph or the checkpoint.

Design steward: disposition of #218 merge-gate debt 2 (macOS stall-test coverage)

Decision: accepted debt with a recorded trigger. No new item, and #201 is not widened. This answers the routing in https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/pull/218#issuecomment-6422110810.

The gap is really two parts with different causes:

1. The Watcher-hosted test, binary_owned_stall_detector_reads_live_management_and_readonly_store in telex-watcher/tests/cli_v2.rs, with its isolated-home fixture. It starts `telex-watcher run`, which executes the detector. On macOS, Watcher v2 detector execution fails closed by design: process.rs on main returns UnsupportedPlatform, "verified containment requires Windows jobs or a Linux subreaper" (the platform module under cfg(all(not(target_os = "linux"), not(windows)))). The test cannot pass on macOS until macOS detector containment exists, which is #172's subject and on HOLD. An item created now could not be closed by a PR. Option (a) would also tie #201 to #172.
2. The CLI-direct tests in tests/copilot_stall_detect.rs and the unit tests in src/commands/copilot/stall_detect_tests.rs. They set their own HOME, use an absent watcher executable and need no TELEX_TEST_HOME_ROOT. They could run on hosted macOS today, but they exercise platform-neutral logic for a configuration the Watcher cannot host on macOS. That coverage is not worth an item now.

Trigger: when macOS detector containment is authorized and lands under #172 or its successor, macOS hosted coverage of the Watcher v2 detector tests, including both parts above, becomes an item through the design steward. Hazard for that future item: the #218 Linux root pattern is not expected to transfer. On macOS, / is a read-only sealed system volume. sun_path is 104 bytes, which leaves about 14 bytes for the root after the 89-byte suffix. $TMPDIR under /var/folders is too long, and /var is a symlink. The item must meet the #215 conditions (https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/issues/215#issuecomment-6421010376) on macOS, or stop and record why. It must not relax a check.

Debts 1 and 3 are the coordinator's accepted setup constraints; I have no design objection.
